questions.question: Indian Standard Time (IST) is ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 hours 30 minutes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Indian Standard Time (IST) is ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) by **5 hours 30 minutes.**
 
• IST is calculated based on the **82.5°E longitude**, which passes through** Mirzapur, near Allahabad in Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• The city of Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, is situated on the** longitude reference line of 82.5°E**, making it the** reference point for calculating Indian Standard Time.**
 
• The **CSIR-National Physical Laboratory (NPL) in New Delhi** is responsible for maintaining and recording time in India. It utilizes **five caesium atomic clocks** for accurate timekeeping.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Greenwich Mean Time (GMT)**

 
 
• It is a time standard based on the location of the prime meridian at the** Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London, England.**
 
• GMT serves as the** basis for the division of the world into different time zones.** It is used as a** reference point **to determine the time offset in relation to the prime meridian.
 
• GMT is often used interchangeably with **Coordinated Universal Time (UTC).** UTC is a more precise and scientifically accurate time standard that incorporates leap seconds to account for Earth's irregular rotation.
 
• GMT was historically used as the** international civil time standard,** particularly during the **era of maritime navigation**. It allowed for uniformity in timekeeping across different regions of the world.

questions.question: Cotton requires ______ temperature, light rainfall or irrigation, ______ frost-free days and bright sun-shine for its growth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**high, 210.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cotton thrives in **high temperatures**, which promotes** optimal growth and development.**
 
• It requires l**ight rainfall **or proper irrigation to provide the necessary moisture for its growth.
 
• Cotton cultivation requires a significant number of frost-free days,** typically around 210, **to ensure the plant's survival and uninterrupted growth.
 
• **Bright sunshine** is crucial for cotton plants as they require ample sunlight for photosynthesis, which is essential for their growth and the production of cotton fibres.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif crops**

 
 
• Kharif Crops are** planted at the onset of the South-West monsoon,** primarily in** India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh,** during the rainy season. 
 
• The sowing of these crops takes place between the months of **June and July. **
 
• Upon reaching maturity, typically in October, these crops are **harvested in the Autumn season. **
 
• Examples of Kharif crops include **rice, cotton, corn, sugarcane, turmeric, pigeon pea, and more.**
 
 
 
• **Rabi crops**
 
 
• Rabi Crops are** cultivated during the winter season **in regions with a subtropical climate.
 
• They include important crops like **wheat, barley, oats, chickpeas, and peas.**
 
• The **Sowing of Rabi crops** takes place between **October and December**.
 
• These crops** require cooler temperatures and lesser rainfall** compared to Kharif crops.
 
• Rabi crops play a crucial role in ensuring food security and contribute significantly to the agricultural economy.
 
 
 
• **Zaid crops**
 
 
• Zaid Crops are **grown during the summer season** in regions with a **tropical climate**.
 
• These crops are typically** cultivated between the months of March and June.**
 
• Zaid crops are known for their **quick growth and shorter duration** compared to Kharif and Rabi crops.
 
• Examples of Zaid crops include **cucumber, watermelon, bitter gourd, and cowpea.**
 
• These crops are often irrigated using modern techniques and are harvested before the onset of the monsoon season.

questions.question: Muscles are of three types. Which of the following is NOT one of them?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sesamoids.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Sesamoids are **small, round bones** embedded within certain tendons, primarily **found in the hands, feet, and knee joints.**
 
• They** provide mechanical support,** improve joint stability, and assist in transmitting forces in the body.
 
• Prominent sesamoid bones include the **patella (kneecap),** two sesamoids located under the** big toe (tibial and fibular sesamoids),** and sesamoids in the **hand's flexor tendons.**
 
• Sesamoids **act as protective cushions, reducing friction and stress** on the tendons they are associated with.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cardiac Muscles**

 
 
• ​​These are specialized muscle tissue found **only in the heart,** responsible for **pumping blood **throughout the body.
 
• Cardiac muscles are** involuntarily controlled by the autonomic nervous system, ensuring continuous and rhythmic contractions.**
 
• Its cells have a **striated or striped appearance **due to the arrangement of **contractile proteins.**
 
• The unique features of cardiac muscle, intercalated discs, **allow cells to communicate and synchronize contractions** for efficient pumping action.
 
• Cardiac muscle exhibits **exceptional endurance and fatigue resistance,** enabling the heart to continuously perform its pumping function.
 
 
 
• **Skeletal Muscles**
 
 
• These muscles attached to the skeleton **enable body movements and provide structural support.**
 
• Skeletal muscles are under** conscious control, allowing individuals to initiate and control their movements**.
 
• They not only enable movement but also **help maintain posture, stabilize joints, and generate body heat.**
 
• Skeletal muscles are connected to bones through **tough, fibrous connective tissues called tendons.​**
 
 
 
• **Smooth Muscles**
 
 
• These are **involuntary muscles** found in the **walls of organs, blood vessels, and other structures** throughout the body.
 
• Smooth muscles are** not under conscious control **and are** regulated by the autonomic nervous system.**
 
• Smooth muscle cells** lack the striped appearance of striated muscles,** as they do not have organized sarcomeres.
 
• They contract and relax slowly, providing sustained contractions for processes like **digestion and blood vessel constriction.**
 
• These muscles are often arranged in layers, allowing for coordinated contractions that **help propel substances through organs and regulate blood flow.**

**Formula used:**

Profit = Selling price - Cost price

Loss = Cost price - Selling price

Profit percentage = Profit/Cost price x 100

Loss percentage = Loss/Cost price x 100

The profit on the first spectacle is Rs. 4,000 x 30/100 = Rs. 1,200.

The total cost of the three spectacles is Rs. 4000 + Rs. 4000 + Rs. 4000 = Rs. 12,000.

The total selling price of the three spectacles is Rs.5200 + Rs. 3,600 + Rs. 3,600 = Rs. 12,400.

The total profit earned in the whole transaction is Rs. 12,400 - Rs. 12,000 = Rs. 400.
